boundaries.contract: Lease initialization precedes listener creation and occurs only with active local DHCP, not DNS-only or relay-only.
Writable startup opens a+ and creates a missing file with umask; default path fallback and option override are explicit.
Missing parent is EC_FILE, before PID/listener side effects.
A directory pathname fails a+ open with EISDIR/EC_FILE.
Unreadable/unwritable inode at startup is EC_FILE.
Read-only filesystem rejects a+ even for readable existing data.
Relative symlink follows target and preserves symlink on writes.
Absolute symlink resolves within image root.
Dangling leaf symlink creates its target if parent exists.
Symlink loop rejects startup with ELOOP.
Open inode persists across rename/replacement; updates do not reopen pathname.
leasefile-ro without script never opens/reads the configured database.
leasefile-ro script init restores a streamed DB; configured file remains untouched.
Script init duplicate records consume independent capacity before pruning.
All C scanf ASCII spaces cross lines, including vertical tab/form feed.
255/64/255/764 widths split oversized tokens across subsequent fields.
Embedded NUL truncates string interpretation but consumes the entire scanned token.
A lone first token reports unclean parse but daemon keeps preceding records.
A two-to-four-field EOF tail warns invalid line then succeeds at EOF.
Invalid/IPv6 addresses (NO_DHCP6 image) warn and skip without taking capacity.
Invalid HW hex empties HW identity; omitted type defaults to Ethernet only with nonzero length.
Typed HW, compact/odd groups, separators, wildcards, 16/255 truncation match aliasing C parser.
Invalid/empty client IDs restore as absent; star skips parser.
atol prefix/sign/signed saturation casts preserve finite negative/0/infinite behavior.
Expiry at/before now prunes after reading, with independent delete events and persisted rewrite.
Nearest finite expiry triggers idle prune/file/DNS/helper maintenance without DHCP traffic.
Every syntactically valid stored row counts before expiry pruning; too many stored leases is EC_MISC.
Duplicate addresses are independently allocated; capacity exhaustion is not bypassed by deduplication.
Invalid addresses do not consume lease slots.
All duplicate addresses survive restoration independently in newest-first order.
Client-ID matches newest-first before HW fallback; duplicate IDs on distinct addresses retain all records.
HW fallback requires missing CLID on at least one side and nonempty HW; type participates.
An older same-address client renews its selected object, preserving the newer client's identity and expiry.
RELEASE removes only the identity-selected object; wrong client has no deletion authority.
DECLINE removes only the matching selected object.
INFORM keeps selected client object for interface/remaining-expiry response.
Newest restored short name steals prior non-authoritative name with old-name notification ordering.
dhcp-fqdn defers FQDN generation and permits equal restored short names until domain scope is known.
Static host configuration applies to each identity-selected lease independently on startup/HUP.
DNS consumes all active leases in C order; forward names and reverse duplicate precedence are preserved.
Agent/vendor extension applies to newest existing address; before-row/invalid-address/invalid-hex ignored.
Extension rows persist after all basic records in newest-first per-record order.
HUP updates config-derived names and schedules OLD; it does not re-read replaced leasefile content.
Restart restores every persisted record with reversed in-file list ordering and identical active ownership.
Failed truncation/write/flush/sync keeps dirty state and schedules 60-second retry without rollback.
Real partial read error is fatal EC_FILE even after earlier valid records.
--dhcp-leasefile without optional argument resets to default; separate next argv is not its value.
--dhcp-lease requires an argument and uses shared canonical occurrence identity.
-l requires an argument; empty explicit value resets default.
Aliases share duplicate-option tracking and CLI/file origin precedence.
